items.summary: Some of the world's biggest oil traders are asking Washington for permission to put sanctioned tankers back to work, as a global vessel shortage pushes oil transportation costs to extraordinary levels. items.summary: For much of the past decade, energy debates often pitted fossil fuels against clean energy. items.title: U.S. Oil, Gas Drillers See Minor Uptick as Oil Prices Crash
items.summary: The total number of active drilling rigs for oil and gas in the United States rose slightly this week, according to new data that Baker Hughes published on Friday, with the total rig count in the US rising to 604, up 56 from this same time last year. The number of active oil rigs rose by 1, to 463 during the latest reporting period, according to the data. This is 49 above this same time last year.…

items.summary: India’s state-owned Oil and Natural Gas Corp. (ONGC) is negotiating to take over operations at two Venezuelan oil projects within six months, a move that could give it control over production and sales at fields where it is owed more than $500 million in dividends. items.summary: For more than half a century, Norway’s oil and gas production has been underpinned by a handful of very large discoveries, the last of which, Wisting in the Barents Sea, was made more than a decade ago. items.title: IEA Sees 4,800 GW of New Renewables by 2031
items.summary: The Strait of Hormuz crisis and the spike in fuel prices are pushing faster renewable energy deployment across the world, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said in a new report on Friday. items.title: Energy Aspects Slashes Forecast of China’s November Diesel Exports
items.summary: Reduced domestic inventories will likely result in significantly lower Chinese exports of diesel in November amid the global diesel crisis, analysts at Energy Aspects say as they slashed their estimates of Chinese shipments this month.
